thread:
sanjay patel: Hey team — just married last week and trying to add my spouse who lives in India to health + dental. Quick Qs: can we do a midyear add for an international spouse? Do you need an apostille/translation for the marriage cert? Also curious how payroll proration works if we pick an effective date retro to the marriage date. Thanks!

emily (People Ops): Congrats, @sanjay! You can add a spouse as a QLE for marriage. We need a copy of the marriage certificate + spouse ID. For foreign docs we accept either a certified English translation OR an apostille; a scanned PDF is fine. Upload everything to the dependent add portal: https://benefits.redwood.com/forms/dependent-add — pick "Marriage" as the QLE reason. You have 30 days from the date of marriage to enroll without an exception.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: midyear QLE evidence must be submitted for review. If more than 30 days, submit an exception request with supporting docs; approvals vary. See: https://benefits.redwood.com/qle-policy :information_source:

liam: quick follow-up — payroll deductions: do they prorate from the coverage effective date or from the next payroll? also any carrier waiting periods for an international add?

emily (People Ops): Payroll prorates based on the coverage effective date. If you request an effective date that is retro to the marriage date (within the allowed QLE window), payroll may apply a retro adjustment on the next pay run to capture the correct deduction. If effective date starts mid-pay-period we'll calculate per-pay-period prorate. Carriers generally don't impose additional "waiting periods" for a QLE spouse add, but some overseas enrollments can take 7–14 business days to process on the carrier side — coverage is typically effective as of the date you request (or marriage date if within 30 days).

emily (People Ops): For filenames please use: surname_firstname_marriage_cert.pdf and surname_firstname_spouse_passport.pdf — makes it easier for us to match. If you need us to submit on your behalf, @sanjay, drop the files here or DM and we'll take care of the portal upload. :thumbsup:

sanjay patel: Thanks — I'll upload tonight. One more: do we need translations notarized or just certified?

emily (People Ops): Certified translation is fine (translator statement + translator signature). Notarization isn't required unless the carrier specifically asks for it, which is uncommon. If the carrier asks later we'll follow up with you.

sanjay patel: Uploaded the two PDFs to the portal and pinged you via DM, @emily. Appreciate the help! :smile:
